title: Eurovision Bars Warring Countries From Hosting
excerpt: The change comes after several European countries boycotted this year’s competition over the inclusion of Israel.
content_html:
Eurovision, the world’s biggest international song contest, will no longer allow countries at war to host the competition.

The winning country typically hosts the next year’s competition, but under the new rules, the winning country will “automatically be ineligible to host the contest if an armed conflict, a sensitive geopolitical situation, or any other situation materially affects the security, safety or stability of their state or immediate region,” Eurovision song contest organizers announced on Wednesday.

The change comes after several European countries boycotted this year’s competition over the inclusion of Israel. Israel came second in both the 2025 and 2026 contests, raising questions about whether it would be allowed to host if it won.

The contest’s governing body approved the amendment after receiving feedback from participating broadcasters.

“These changes are about giving everyone involved greater clarity, protecting artists and ensuring the contest continues to provide a safe and welcoming environment, while preserving the spirit and integrity that make the Eurovision Song Contest so special,” Martin Green, director of the Eurovision Song Contest, said in a statement.

Eurovision organizers made several more changes to the competition’s rules, including raising the minimum age for performers as of the first day of rehearsal from 16 to 18.

Controversy

Five countries—Spain, Iceland, Ireland, the Netherlands, and Slovenia—boycotted this year’s competition in Vienna, Austria, in May after the European Broadcasting Union refused calls to suspend Israel from the contest. Ireland’s public broadcaster RTÉ said in a September statement that its “participation would be unconscionable given the ongoing and appalling loss of lives in Gaza.” José Pablo López, president of Spain’s public broadcaster RTVE, said that same month that “it was about time to break the silence within the EBU regarding the genocide in Gaza.”

Broadcasters also argued that the competitors of Eurovision are not ordinary performers but representatives of their nations. Eurovision “is not merely a song contest,” López said. It’s “the most politicized festival in existence.”

The broadcasters’ decision to withdraw from the contest marked the largest multinational political boycott in Eurovision history.

The boycott came amid intense backlash from the public over the inclusion of Israel in the competition despite its military occupation and bombardment of Gaza, which has killed more than 73,000 people since Oct. 7, 2023.

Israel has participated in Eurovision since 1973, becoming the first non-European country to join the competition. Because Eurovision is run by public broadcasters that are part of the EBU, it includes EBU members outside Europe, such as Canada, which will be eligible to participate in the song contest in 2027 after its broadcaster joined the union in 2026. Bulgaria is set to host the 2027 competition.

But Israel’s inclusion in recent years raised questions about whether the competition was taking a consistent stance towards countries at war. Eurovision banned Russia from participating in the contest after it invaded Ukraine in February 2022, arguing that its inclusion would bring the contest into disrepute. Later that year, the EBU indefinitely suspended Russian state broadcasters from its governance and membership.

After Israel finished second in both the 2025 and 2026 contests—results that also drew scrutiny over allegations of government interference, which the country denied—some broadcasters reportedly expressed safety concerns if the contest were to be hosted there in the future. (An investigation by Eurovision News Spotlight found that the Israeli government had funded an extensive online campaign for its 2025 entry. The EBU maintained that the result was valid but introduced new restrictions this year prohibiting disproportionate promotion, including state-backed campaigns. It formally warned Israeli broadcaster KAN over videos urging viewers to cast all 10 of their votes for Israel. The broadcaster denied wrongdoing and the EBU said the videos did not affect the results of the competition.)

Eurovision has moved competitions before due to geopolitical issues, although there has not been a formal rule until now. Ukraine hosted Eurovision in 2017 in spite of fighting between Ukrainian forces and Moscow-backed separatists in the east. The country won again in 2022, but the 2023 competition was ultimately hosted in Liverpool, U.K., on Ukraine’s behalf.

The new rule also institutionalizes a process to determine whether a winning country not at war is eligible to host. The EBU said it could commission an independent security assessment to determine whether a winning country can safely host the event, and if not, the EBU will appoint another host country.

Under the new rules, an appointed host country would also organize the contest “in its own right” and “will not be required to stage the event on behalf of another member.” That change differs from the 2023 competition for which British and Ukrainian broadcasters collaborated on the production of the competition.

content_html_zh:
世界上最大的国际歌曲大赛欧洲歌唱大赛将不再允许交战国家主办比赛。

欧洲歌唱大赛组织者周三宣布，获胜国家通常会主办明年的比赛，但根据新规则，如果武装冲突、敏感的地缘政治局势或任何其他情况严重影响其国家或邻近地区的安全、保障或稳定，获胜国家将“自动失去主办比赛的资格”。

这一变化是在几个欧洲国家抵制今年因以色列加入而举行的比赛之后发生的。 以色列在 2025 年和 2026 年的比赛中均获得第二名，引发了人们对如果以色列获胜是否可以主办该国的疑问。

竞赛管理机构在收到参与广播公司的反馈后批准了修正案。

欧洲歌唱大赛总监马丁·格林（Martin Green）在一份声明中表示：“这些变化是为了让每个参与者都更加清晰，保护艺术家并确保比赛继续提供一个安全和热情的环境，同时保留使欧洲歌唱大赛如此特别的精神和诚信。”

欧洲电视网组织者对比赛规则进行了更多修改，包括将排练第一天表演者的最低年龄从 16 岁提高到 18 岁。

争议

欧洲广播联盟拒绝禁止以色列参加比赛的呼吁后，西班牙、冰岛、爱尔兰、荷兰和斯洛文尼亚等五个国家抵制了今年在奥地利维也纳举行的比赛。 爱尔兰公共广播公司 RTÉ 在 9 月份的一份声明中表示，“鉴于加沙地带持续发生令人震惊的生命损失，其参与是不合理的”。 西班牙公共广播公司 RTVE 总裁若泽·巴勃罗·洛佩斯 (José Pablo López) 同月表示，“是时候打破 EBU 内部对加沙种族灭绝的沉默了。”

广播公司还辩称，欧洲歌唱大赛的参赛者不是普通表演者，而是各自国家的代表。 洛佩兹说，欧洲歌唱大赛“不仅仅是一场歌曲比赛”。 这是“现存最政治化的节日”。

广播公司退出比赛的决定标志着欧洲电视网历史上最大规模的跨国政治抵制。

此次抵制活动正值公众强烈反对以色列参加竞赛之际，尽管以色列军事占领并轰炸了加沙，自 2023 年 10 月 7 日以来，以色列已造成超过 73,000 人死亡。

以色列自1973年起参加欧洲歌唱大赛，成为第一个参加比赛的非欧洲国家。 由于欧洲歌唱大赛是由属于 EBU 的公共广播公司运营，因此它包括欧洲以外的 EBU 成员，例如加拿大，其广播公司于 2026 年加入联盟后，将有资格参加 2027 年的歌曲比赛。 保加利亚将主办 2027 年的比赛。

但近年来以色列的加入引发了人们的疑问：这项竞赛是否对交战国家采取了一致的立场。 2022 年 2 月俄罗斯入侵乌克兰后，欧洲电视网禁止俄罗斯参加该比赛，认为俄罗斯的加入将使该比赛名誉扫地。 同年晚些时候，EBU 无限期暂停了俄罗斯国家广播公司的治理和会员资格。

以色列在 2025 年和 2026 年的比赛中获得第二名后（该结果也因政府干预指控而受到审查，但该国否认了这一点）据报道，一些广播公司对未来在那里举办比赛表示了安全担忧。 （欧洲电视网新闻聚焦的一项调查发现，以色列政府为其 2025 年参赛项目资助了一场广泛的在线活动。 EBU 坚称结果有效，但今年引入了新的限制，禁止不成比例的促销活动，包括国家支持的活动。 它就敦促观众将全部 10 票投给以色列的视频向以色列广播公司 KAN 发出正式警告。 广播公司否认有不当行为，EBU 表示这些视频不会影响比赛结果。）

欧洲电视网之前曾因地缘政治问题而改变比赛安排，但迄今为止还没有正式的规则。 尽管乌克兰军队与莫斯科支持的东部分裂分子之间发生战斗，乌克兰仍于 2017 年主办了欧洲歌唱大赛。 该国在 2022 年再次获胜，但 2023 年的比赛最终代表乌克兰在英国利物浦举行。

新规则还将确定未发生战争的获胜国家是否有资格主办的程序制度化。 EBU表示，可以委托进行独立的安全评估，以确定获胜国家是否可以安全主办赛事，如果不能，EBU将指定另一个主办国。

根据新规则，指定的主办国也将“以其自身的权利”组织比赛，并且“无需代表其他成员举办比赛”。 这一变化与 2023 年比赛不同，英国和乌克兰广播公司合作制作了比赛。
